## 開篇固定收益主論

美國總統川普取消原定對伊朗發動的攻擊，並表示可能很快宣布終戰協議後，美國公債在6月11日全面上漲。油價隨之走低，市場對聯準會下次升息25個基點的完全定價，也由12月延後至2027年第1季。2年期殖利率下跌8.2個基點至4.063%，5年期下跌9.6個基點至4.185%，10年期下跌9.1個基點至4.462%，30年期則下跌7.4個基點至4.956%。

這波漲勢是在川普發表談話後加速，並非源自明確溫和的經濟數據。5月生產者物價較4月上升1.1%，高於0.7%的市場共識，年增率則為6.5%；扣除食品、能源與貿易服務的指標月增0.8%，同樣超過0.5%的預估。初領失業救濟金人數也高於預期，增添一項勞動市場轉弱訊號，但不足以抵銷通膨數據的意外上行。

協議前景降低了伊朗供應與荷莫茲海峽面臨的即時風險，油價明顯收低。WTI下跌2.58%至$87.71，布蘭特原油下跌2.92%至$90.38。利率市場原本正在評估能源衝擊是否會迫使聯準會再次升息；油價回落後，短期利率合約完全計入升息25個基點的時點，從12月延後至2027年初。

美債上漲同時反映實質殖利率與通膨補償下降。10年期實質殖利率下跌5.5個基點至2.152%，10年期損益兩平通膨率下跌3.6個基點至2.31%，顯示能源通膨溢價與經通膨調整後的報酬要求均降低。不過，兩者都尚未回到1個月前的水準；同期10年期名目殖利率仍上升4.8個基點，實質殖利率上升22.2個基點，損益兩平通膨率則下降17.4個基點。

風險性資產將這項變化解讀為未來成長與通膨組合改善，而非經濟即將急遽轉弱的警訊。標普500指數上漲1.75%，Nasdaq 100上漲3.29%，費城半導體指數大漲7.91%；VIX下跌12.51%至19.44，投資級、高收益與新興市場債券基金也全面上漲。美元指數下跌0.09%，黃金則下滑0.44%。

不過，這波行情仍有幾項限制。川普過去曾稱協議在望，卻未促成持久安排，伊朗是否接受最新條件也尚未確認。批發物價顯示能源成本已沿供應鏈傳導：最終需求商品價格大漲2.8%，就連排除波動較大的食品、能源與貿易利潤的指標也顯著上升。ECB已因同一項全球衝擊升息，為2023年以來首次；聯準會迎接6月會議之際，則同時面對偏高的美國通膨、僅逐步轉弱的勞動市場，以及新任主席尚不明朗的溝通策略。

## 油價回落蓋過生產者物價高漲

生產者物價漲勢相當廣泛，使美債市場最初對經濟數據的反應受到限制。5月最終需求價格月增1.1%，與4月相同，年增率升至6.5%；月增幅高於0.7%的市場共識，而且並非由單一狹窄類別造成。

商品價格上漲2.8%，其中能源價格大漲10.7%；服務價格上升0.3%。扣除食品、能源與貿易服務的指標繼4月上升0.5%後，5月月增0.8%，高於0.5%的共識，年增率達5.1%。這些數據進一步顯示，能源衝擊已不只反映於原油本身，也正傳入美國國內的生產與配送成本。

這種組成不如稍早公布的消費者物價報告令人安心，後者的核心通膨增幅低於預期。數據並未證明批發物價漲幅將全數轉嫁給消費者，卻使聯準會在6月16日至17日會議前無法獲得一致轉弱的通膨序列。消費者與生產者物價的差異，迫使官員判斷溫和的核心消費通膨能否持續，抑或只是尚未反映生產流程成本再度上升。

勞動數據是當日美國國內最主要的反向訊號。截至6月6日當週，初領失業救濟金人數增加4,000人至22.9萬人，高於22萬人的市場共識，並創2月以來最高；4週移動平均由21萬4,750人升至21.9萬人。截至5月30日當週，續領人數增加2.4萬人至179.5萬人，前值則修正為177.1萬人；受保失業率維持在1.2%。

這些數據顯示，新裁員與求職所需時間都略有惡化，但幅度尚不足以證明勞動需求已明顯轉折。其重要性在於重新平衡聯準會的雙重使命：通膨面出現顯著上行意外，就業面則是壓力逐步增加，而非足以讓緊縮政策失去可能性的驟然疲弱。

川普對伊朗立場的轉變，對市場定價的影響更為強烈。當天稍早，他曾威脅若德黑蘭不接受臨時協議，將進一步攻擊並奪取伊朗石油基礎設施；其後取消原定當晚發動的攻擊，表示談判內容已送達伊朗領導層，並稱將公布簽署協議的時間與地點。不過，相關報導未能證實德黑蘭已批准最終文本，外交突破仍有逆轉風險。

川普宣布消息前，各天期美債殖利率僅下跌約2個基點；消息公布後，油價盤中跌逾3%，各天期殖利率隨後下降8至11個基點，回到6月5日強勁的5月就業報告促使投資人轉向更鷹派聯準會路徑之前的水準。

由於消息同時影響政策預期與較長天期的通膨風險，殖利率曲線的反應相對有限。2年期與10年期利差收窄0.9個基點至39.9個基點，2年期與30年期利差則擴大0.8個基點至89.3個基點。5年期領漲，但各附息券天期間的差距太小，不足以顯示曲線中的政策與期限溢價成分已全面重整。

損益兩平通膨率下降與油價走低一致，但實質殖利率跌幅更大，顯示行情不只是機械式剔除能源溢價。地緣政治風險降低，提高了聯準會可以等待、而不必在全球經濟放緩之際進一步收緊政策的可能性。股市同步上漲也支持這項解讀：投資人降低了持續通膨、政策趨緊與經濟活動受阻同時出現的機率。

這份舒緩仍有條件。WTI與布蘭特原油本週及本月均下跌，但收盤價仍接近$88與$90，能源成本依舊可觀。生產者物價則顯示，先前的漲幅已進入商品價格與範圍更廣的基礎指標。若正式簽署協議並重新開放受阻的貿易路線，未來通膨壓力可望下降，卻不會逆轉已發生的價格上漲，也不能保證企業不再把成本轉嫁出去。

世界銀行更新的全球展望凸顯了其中的經濟利害。由於戰爭干擾商品流動並推升能源與進口成本，世銀下調了三分之二經濟體的評估，預測2026年全球經濟成長2.5%，為2020年疫情衰退以來最弱。中國與印度以外的新興經濟體惡化幅度最大，中國成長預測則由4.4%下調至4.2%。

世銀將這次事件形容為50多年來最大的供給衝擊，並表示若能源供應受阻情況惡化，又同時出現嚴重金融壓力，全球成長率可能降至1.3%。這些是有條件的估算，並非預測悲觀情境必然發生；但也說明即使最新美國數據仍強到不足以支持寬鬆政策，一份可信的和平協議仍可透過通膨與實質利率兩條管道壓低殖利率。

## 長債供給遇上聯準會流動性後盾

在地緣政治因素帶動的漲勢加速前，美國財政部標售$220億的30年期增額債券，需求訊號好壞參半。最高得標殖利率為5.020%，低於5月新券的5.046%，但高於標售前交易顯示的水準。投標倍數由2.30升至2.33，不過得標殖利率高於標售前水準，顯示投資人仍要求標售讓利。

配售結果較為正面。直接投標人取得獲接受競爭性投標的25.31%，間接投標人取得59.95%，一級交易商承接14.74%。直接投標人的占比協助市場吸收這筆$220億增額發行，其規模小於5月的$250億新券。債券票息為5.000%，6月15日交割，2056年5月15日到期。

標售結果公布後，殖利率一度上升，但這波回檔很快被油價帶動的債市漲勢蓋過。30年期殖利率盤中最多下跌9個基點，收盤回到5%以下。這段走勢區分了標售本身與當日主要重定價因素：需求雖弱於標售前交易所暗示的程度，卻沒有差到足以抵擋地緣政治與通膨前景大幅改變所帶來的影響。

短端標售未顯示普遍性的融資壓力。財政部$700億4週期國庫券的最高得標利率為3.595%，低於前次3.615%，投標倍數則由3.07升至3.13。間接投標人取得70.59%，直接投標人取得2.01%，交易商承接27.39%。這筆規模較小的發行將於6月16日交割、7月14日到期。

$750.01億的8週期國庫券標售利率維持在3.610%，但投標倍數由3.20降至2.94。間接投標人占比仍高達69.59%，直接投標人取得2.27%，交易商承接28.14%；同樣於6月16日交割，8月11日到期。4週期需求改善、8週期投標倍數轉弱，顯示兩筆標售不應被視為一致的流動性訊號。

聯準會的準備金管理操作帶來另一項融資市場發展。紐約聯準銀行表示，在截至7月13日的每月操作期間內，將買進約$100億國庫券，與前一週期相同，另進行約$165億的再投資買進。在國庫券供給預料增加、政府現金餘額將升破$1兆前，這項決定可繼續支撐準備金水準。

聯準會在結束量化緊縮後，於12月開始每月買進約$400億國庫券，4月將速度降至$250億，5月再降至$100億。此次維持買進額，代表先前快速放慢的步調暫停，但不表示將回到早先的規模。紐約聯準銀行市場主管Roberto Perli曾表示，為維持充裕準備金，買進規模可向上或向下調整。

目前融資環境仍屬寬鬆。截至6月10日當週，銀行準備金增加$658億至$3.111兆，高於2025年底的$2.85兆；貨幣市場基金資產創新高，相較於可用擔保品，市場現金仍相當充裕。因此，維持買進屬預防性安排，目的是因應財政部現金管理未來可能造成的準備金流失，而非回應已發生的市場失靈。

殖利率下跌之際，現券美債交易活動增加。FINRA記錄的面額交易量為$1.188兆，共415,918筆，較前一交易日增加6.8%。名目附息債交易量成長13.3%至$9,264億，其中剩餘期限超過3年至5年的債券增加24.6%，超過7年至10年的區段增加31.4%；TIPS交易量則減少33%至$319億。

成交量顯示這波漲勢發生在交易活躍的時段，尤其集中於曲線中段與指標10年期區段，但總量數據無法判斷客戶是淨買方或淨賣方。價格提供了更明確的結論：伊朗消息改變市場對能源衝擊持續時間的預期，因此壓過偏熱的通膨數據、略顯疲弱的長債標售結果，以及大量附息債交易。

## ECB展開新一輪升息循環

ECB將存款利率上調25個基點至2.25%，這是近3年來首次升息，也是主要央行首次以緊縮政策回應伊朗相關能源衝擊。決策獲得一致支持，也大致符合預期，因此總裁拉加德的說明內容及未來是否繼續升息，才是影響歐洲公債更重要的訊息。

拉加德表示，衝擊正在整體經濟中擴散，直接與間接成本均已浮現；她也否認這次行動屬於預防性升息。ECB認為前景同時面臨通膨上行與成長下行風險，最終影響取決於能源衝擊的持續時間、強度及第二輪傳導程度。

ECB的新預測顯示，消費者物價在2026與2027年的增速將加快，2028年才回到接近2%。拉加德表示，能源價格會在夏季進一步推高通膨，並使其在2027年上半年持續遠高於目標。與此同時，衝突正在壓抑經濟活動，調查也顯示成長放慢，尤其是服務業。

決策公布後，歐洲債券守住漲幅，10年期指標殖利率據報下跌3個基點至3.05%。這項反應並非市場否定升息，而是同時反映近期政策利率路徑上移、未來成長轉弱，以及稍後同樣推動美債上漲的油價下跌。

官員仍保留最早於7月再次升息的可能。市場主流預期仍是等到9月下一輪季度預測公布時行動，但熟悉管理委員會討論的人士表示，若通膨疑慮持續，不能排除7月升息；地緣政治與能源前景若改善，則仍可能暫停。

IMF支持進一步緊縮，但也保留成長方面的條件。其基準情境假設2026年累計升息50個基點，並預測歐元區通膨率為2.8%，高於先前的2.4%。工作人員表示，若後續數據符合基準情境，政策可能需要稍微更具限制性；若能源價格與通膨預期超過基準，則有必要更快或更大幅度升息。

IMF同時把歐元區成長預測由1.1%下調至0.9%，並指出金融環境與需求若出現更大幅度的惡化，可能擴大產出缺口，降低緊縮的必要性。這項條件十分重要，因為ECB面對的是供給衝擊：其通膨效應支持升息，但對家庭購買力與企業活動的拖累又要求央行保持克制。

政治反對聲浪迅速出現。義大利副總理Antonio Tajani表示，升息無助於情勢，並主張當通膨源於外部因素時，信用仍應維持可取得性。義大利也在歐元區財長會議中表達反對；葡萄牙同樣不贊成，其財長雖承認ECB的獨立性，仍稱這項政策訊號沒有必要。

挪威面對類似衝突，但當前政策位置不同。挪威央行的區域網絡調查顯示，企業預期第2季產出成長0.2%、第3季成長0.3%；先前對第2季的預測為0.4%。回報產能受限的企業略為減少，招募困難也有所緩解。

5月核心通膨意外升至4個月高點後，這份調查降低了6月18日會議再次升息的壓力。企業仍預期就業將小幅增加，並把薪資成長預測調高至4.5%，與央行預測相同。因此，數據削弱了連續第2次升息的近期理由，卻未消除支撐升息討論的薪資與進口物價壓力。

英國下次政策決定則增添財政風險。投資人正為6月18日Makerfield補選可能引發的波動做準備；這場選舉可能讓工黨政治人物Andy Burnham進入國會，並可能挑戰首相施凱爾。由於Burnham的財政方針仍難以評估，經理人尤其擔心長天期英國公債。

英國4月預算赤字達£243億，為6年來同月最高；OECD預測，債務占國內生產毛額比率將由2023年的98.8%升至2027年的105.4%。部分投資人認為，30年期英國公債殖利率必須再上升近40個基點、或達到約6%，才能充分補償這項不確定性。若Burnham落敗並增強市場對現行財政規則的信心，債市可能獲得舒緩；但若英國改革黨勝選，則會帶來另一組制度與政策疑問。

## 信用市場獎勵融資規畫明確者，拒絕薄弱結構

企業信用市場仍向大型借款人開放，但反應最佳的是能明確界定未來融資需求，或願意就風險明確付出溢價的發行人。花旗集團旗下銀行部門以4個券次發行$62.5億投資級債券，期限介於2至6年，是其2026年首筆高評級交易。最長券次相對美債的利差由接近95個基點的初步定價討論收窄至67個基點。

這批債券由營運公司Citibank發行，並非控股公司債務，預期評級分別為Moody’s Aa3、S&P A+及Fitch AA-。長期債務資本規則變更後，花旗的發行急迫性下降，因而落後其他已於年內籌得逾$1,200億的華爾街大型銀行。

Oracle的資料中心支出高於預期，導致股價大跌，債券卻逆勢上漲。公司表示，2026曆年內預計不會再舉債，並規畫在新會計年度籌措$400億債務與股權資金，其中包括先前宣布的$200億市價增發股權計畫。

截至紐約時間中午，Oracle票息3.65%、2041年到期債券的利差收窄15個基點至200個基點；票息6.9%、2052年到期債券的利差收窄12個基點至209個基點。5年期違約保護成本最多下降3.4個基點至155.7個基點。

市場的正面反應，是因公司為新增借款劃出較明確的界線，而非資本需求下降。截至5月31日止季度，Oracle支出約$165億，使全年資本支出達$557億，高於原先預測的$500億；新會計年度的淨資本支出預料約為$700億。即使投資計畫規模仍然極大，採用更多客戶預付款，並由客戶自行提供處理器，仍被視為有助降低近期現金需求。

CoreWeave則證明，全球投資需求也延伸至評級較低的AI基礎設施業者。公司發行€20億、6年期歐元債券，殖利率8.5%，另發行$12.5億、6年期美元債券，殖利率9.625%。歐元券訂單超過€70億，成為美國AI基礎設施公司首筆此類歐元計價垃圾債交易。

這筆交易擴大了CoreWeave的融資來源，但未消除其財務風險。公司預計年內投資接近$350億，並消耗近$260億現金。在此次發行前，自2025年5月以來，公司已發行$65億垃圾級美元債券、$66億可轉換債券，以及一筆以客戶晶片合約為擔保的$31億貸款；評級分別為Moody’s Ba3、S&P B+及Fitch BB-。

Hanuman Wind Power則遭遇市場選擇性的另一面。這家泰國Energy Absolute旗下的香港公司把認購期延長1天後，仍第2度推遲擬議中的綠色垃圾債發行。最新債券提供9%區間中高檔的殖利率，但投資人依然擔心母公司的治理問題，以及美債殖利率上升後15年期結構的相對價值。

部分擬募得資金原定提供給Energy Absolute，而泰國市場監管機關已指控其創辦人與前高階主管涉及詐欺。發行人2月也曾延後一筆交易。反覆撤回發行顯示，當市場疑慮集中於治理、對母公司的結構性曝險與過長期限時，接近兩位數的高殖利率及再生能源標籤仍不足以吸引投資人。

印尼主權財富基金Danantara則完成了在該國市場動盪期間備受檢視的首次交易。基金透過各$7.5億的5年期與10年期券次，共籌得$15億。5年期債券以5.35%定價，兩個券次的利差均較初步定價討論收窄約35個基點。

每個券次的需求都不到發行額的2倍，低於近期許多亞洲交易至少3倍的認購水準；但在印尼匯率、股票與本地債券承壓後，能夠完成發行仍是重要的融資成果。債券在後續亞洲交易時段上漲。這筆交易證明Danantara可以取得全球美元資金，但未消除印尼其他資產所反映的政策與治理疑慮。

基金也在考慮以低於市場水準的票息發行本幣債券。這項潛在結構再次引發市場對先前低於市場利率之「愛國者債券」的疑慮，因此，成功完成國際發行與任何由國內政策引導的融資條件之間，仍須明確區分。

其他借款人仍處於較早階段。Dangote Petroleum Refinery正尋求透過面向外國投資人的私募債籌措最多$10億，同時準備首次公開發行股票，並擴建最高日處理量達70萬桶的煉油廠。投資人會議仍在進行，交易尚無法確定。辛巴威則正洽談一筆$1.5億的非洲開發銀行貸款，作為清償欠款並重整約$230億債務之更廣泛計畫的一部分；該國自1999年以來一直被排除於國際資本市場之外。

## 亞洲利率依能源曝險與國內政策可信度分化

印尼本地市場最清楚顯示，全球油價風險下降仍無法立即修復國內信心。週四，指標10年期殖利率上升10個基點至7.45%，接近2022年以來最高水準，5年期殖利率也上升3個基點。印尼盾貶值0.2%，股市指標盤中一度下跌2%，收盤跌幅縮至0.3%。

這波跌勢發生在官員說明捍衛匯率的措施、帶動市場短暫反彈之後。印尼央行已接受更高的債券殖利率、收緊流動性，並自5月以來累計升息75個基點，其中包括一次會期間升息25個基點。分析師仍認為還有25至50個基點的升息空間，市場普遍預期6月18日例會將再次行動。

年內外國投資人已從印尼股票淨撤出$39億，並從債券撤出$5.97億。印尼盾兌美元貶值約7%，股價指數跌逾30%。高油價威脅貿易收支與通膨前景，但市場持續疲弱，也反映投資人對財政政策、治理及總統普拉伯沃干預式施政方針的疑慮。

Danantara完成美元發債、印尼盾隨後回升，顯示信心並非全面消失。意外升息後，印尼盾寫下10月以來最佳單週表現，並升破兌1美元18,000印尼盾關卡；印尼股市週五也上漲。不過，這波復甦是在市場嚴重下跌後出現，仍不足以消除本地公債市場對更高殖利率與更明確政策的要求。

泰國呈現不同的區域利率格局。其10年期殖利率比2年期高近110個基點，曲線陡峭程度接近新興亞洲之最，利差也接近2022年11月以來最大。與為捍衛匯率而緊縮的國家不同，泰國經濟疲弱、5月通膨轉軟，讓投資人預期泰國央行將延長暫停升息的期間。

外國投資人本季已買進約$3.42億泰國債券，收復3月約$10億資金流出的一部分。10年期殖利率也已從5月觸及的逾1年高點2.4%回落。Bloomberg模型估計，自衝突升級以來該殖利率上升近60個基點，目前約高於公允價值40個基點；相較之下，美債殖利率、美元、區域股市與油價所能解釋的幅度約為18個基點。

這項估值來自模型，並非已實現的政策訊號，卻仍反映同一區域能源衝擊下，泰國長債為何可能與印尼債券走勢不同。泰銖交換市場尚未在未來6個月內完全反映升息25個基點，但印度與南韓交換利率已至少反映50個基點的緊縮幅度。

祕魯在政治不確定性之中也維持政策穩定。央行連續第9個月把基準利率維持在4.25%，符合13名經濟學家的預期，另有1人原先預測升息25個基點。利馬通膨率由4.01%放緩至3.91%，支持央行認為國內天然氣短缺、全球油價及農作物受損帶來的壓力可能只是暫時性的看法，但通膨仍高於1%至3%的目標區間。

總統決選在開票98.2%後仍無結果，Keiko Fujimori與Roberto Sánchez之間相差不到1,000票。數十萬張遭質疑的選票可能使正式結果延至7月。政治不確定性本週影響匯率，但央行維持利率，仍使貨幣政策決定與尚未落幕的選舉有所區隔。

日本6月會議依舊十分重要，但總裁植田和男預計缺席，使市場焦點由可能的利率決策轉向溝通方式。植田預計以聲明表達看法但不參與投票，副總裁冰見野良三將代理主席，另一位副總裁內田真一則預定主持記者會。

隔夜指數交換一度把升息25個基點的機率降至約73%，隨後又回到接近完全定價。投資人因此未把植田住院視為預期利率決策的根本改變。不確定性在於內田能否清楚說明後續緊縮的可能性與速度，這項差異將直接影響日圓與超長天期JGB。

## 前瞻市場意義

美國近期首項考驗是6月12日美東時間10:00公布的密西根大學初步調查。消費者信心指數預計由5月終值44.8升至46.1；在生產者物價出現廣泛月增、油價又因外交希望而下跌後，其中的家庭通膨預期對利率市場更為重要。預期下降將支持能源衝擊尚未固化的判斷；若預期再度上升，市場損益兩平通膨率雖已下滑，聯準會仍難以因此感到安心。

英國4月國內生產毛額將於6月12日稍早公布，市場預期繼3月成長0.3%後，月減0.1%。數據將更新英格蘭銀行6月18日決策中的經濟活動面資訊，也有助英國公債市場評估：當能源通膨與國內政治風險仍高時，經濟還能承受多少政策限制。

美國6月15日公布工業生產，預期5月繼前月成長0.9%後增加0.1%；產能利用率前值為76.1%。這是FOMC會議前最後一項主要實體經濟活動數據。同日，財政部將交割$580億3年期、$390億10年期及$220億30年期債券，附息債總交割額達$1,190億；另將標售$890億13週期與$770億26週期國庫券，與這項資產負債表事件一同考驗短端吸收能力。

中國將於6月16日公布5月工業生產、零售銷售與固定資產投資。前值分別為工業生產年增4.1%、零售銷售成長3.2%，以及固定資產投資年初至今下降1.6%。整組數據將顯示，中國內需與財政政策傳導是否足以抵銷外部能源與貿易衝擊對中國及區域債市的影響。

日本央行在6月15日至16日會議後，將於16日公布決策。市場普遍預期升息25個基點至約1%，但更大的考驗，是植田未出席記者會時的政策指引。若明確傳達後續仍將緊縮，可能加重JGB的壓力，並放大利差對日圓的影響；若訊息模糊，則會提高這項已被市場高度反映之決策所帶來的波動。

澳洲央行也將於6月16日決策；5月升息後，維持利率於4.35%是基準預期。美國則在美東時間08:30公布進出口物價與新屋開工，隨後標售$650億6週期國庫券及增額發行$130億20年期公債。貿易物價可顯示能源與商品衝擊是否正在擴大；30年期增額債最高得標殖利率高於標售前指示水準後，20年期標售將再度檢驗長天期債券需求。

6月17日美東時間08:30公布5月零售銷售，之後FOMC於14:00發布決策，主席Kevin Warsh並於14:30舉行上任後首場會後記者會。零售銷售預計在4月初值成長0.5%後，再增加0.5%至0.6%。若消費保持韌性、生產者物價又維持強勁，市場把完全反映升息的時間推遲至2027年的定價將更難獲得支持；若消費轉弱，則會呼應失業救濟金數據，並強化實質殖利率下降所反映的成長舒緩。

聯準會預計維持3.50%至3.75%的目標區間，因此經濟預測摘要與Warsh的溝通將成為主要焦點。投資人將觀察新主席是否保留利率點陣圖與既有程度的前瞻指引，以及他如何連結資產負債表政策與利率前景。即使決策本身不變，溝通資訊減少仍可能提高波動。

6月18日將有印尼央行、瑞士國家銀行、挪威央行、英格蘭銀行及菲律賓央行公布決策。印尼會議將檢驗央行在會期間出手捍衛印尼盾後，是否會從5.50%再升息25個基點。挪威央行必須權衡企業活動放緩、仍強勁的核心通膨與4.5%的薪資成長預期；英格蘭銀行則須同時評估能源通膨、成長轉弱及Makerfield選舉結果。

在這些判斷形成前，油價仍是最可能改變全局的條件。若正式簽署協議並實質減少供應中斷，能源通膨將進一步下降，各國央行也能更依本國成長與薪資情況採取不同政策。若談判破裂，市場將重回週四漲勢前的組合：原油價格高漲、生產流程通膨擴散，而且即使全球前景轉弱，進一步緊縮的壓力仍然存在。

overall_summary.headline: 伊朗外交進展與油價下跌蓋過生產者物價廣泛飆升，美債走高
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國總統川普取消原定對伊朗發動的攻擊，並表示可能很快宣布終戰協議後，美國公債全面上漲。2年期殖利率下跌8.2個基點至4.063%，5年期下跌9.6個基點至4.185%，10年期下跌9.1個基點至4.462%，30年期則下跌7.4個基點至4.956%。WTI下跌2.58%至$87.71，布蘭特原油下跌2.92%至$90.38，使市場完全反映聯準會下次升息的時點由12月延後至2027年第1季。

這波漲勢克服的是廣泛的通膨上行意外，並非由溫和數據帶動。5月生產者物價月增1.1%、年增6.5%，扣除食品、能源與貿易服務的指標則上升0.8%。初領失業救濟金人數增至22.9萬人，增添勞動市場轉弱的訊號，但尚未證明需求已明顯轉折。油價下跌壓低通膨補償，實質殖利率跌幅更大，則反映聯準會更有空間等待，而不必在全球經濟放緩之際進一步緊縮。

投資人降低了持續通膨、政策趨緊與經濟活動受阻的風險評估，帶動股市上漲、波動率下降。不過，舒緩仍有條件：伊朗是否批准最終協議尚未獲證實，先前的能源漲價已開始進入生產成本，ECB也因通膨壓力擴散而升息25個基點。
overall_summary.summary: 川普取消原定對伊朗發動的攻擊並暗示協議將近後，美債殖利率下跌7.4至9.6個基點；即使5月生產者物價漲幅高於預期，能源通膨溢價仍隨之下降。

section_summaries.market_read: 這波漲勢同時反映能源通膨溢價下降，以及經通膨調整後的報酬要求降低。
section_summaries.summary: 伊朗外交進展取代生產者物價衝擊，成為當日行情的主導因素，推動美債殖利率大幅下降，並使市場完全反映聯準會下次升息的時點延後至2027年第1季。10年期實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率同步下跌，股市則上漲、波動率下降，顯示市場對能源通膨、政策趨緊與成長轉弱並存的前景有所舒緩。

section_summaries.market_read: 油價下跌壓低損益兩平通膨率；即使生產流程通膨仍強，地緣政治風險緩解也讓聯準會有更多等待空間。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied broadly on June 11 after President Donald Trump canceled planned strikes against Iran and said an agreement to end the war could soon be announced, driving oil lower and pushing expectations for the next fully priced Federal Reserve increase into the first quarter of 2027. The 2-year yield fell 8.2 basis points to 4.063%, the 5-year dropped 9.6 basis points to 4.185%, the 10-year declined 9.1 basis points to 4.462% and the 30-year shed 7.4 basis points to 4.956%.

The rally gathered force after Trump’s announcement, rather than emerging from an unambiguously benign economic release. May producer prices rose 1.1% from April, above the 0.7% consensus, and 6.5% from a year earlier. A measure excluding food, energy and trade services increased 0.8% on the month, also exceeding its 0.5% estimate. Initial jobless claims simultaneously rose more than expected, adding a softer labor signal but not erasing the inflation surprise.

Oil settled decisively lower as the prospect of an agreement reduced the immediate risk around Iranian supply and the Strait of Hormuz. WTI fell 2.58% to $87.71 and Brent lost 2.92% to $90.38. The shift mattered directly for a rates market that had been debating whether the energy shock would require another Fed increase: short-rate contracts moved the point at which a quarter-point hike was fully priced from December into early 2027.

The Treasury move combined lower real yields with lower inflation compensation. The 10-year real yield declined 5.5 basis points to 2.152%, while the 10-year breakeven fell 3.6 basis points to 2.31%. That split showed both a reduced energy-inflation premium and a lower inflation-adjusted return requirement, though neither component returned to its level of a month earlier. The 10-year nominal yield was still 4.8 basis points higher over that period and the real yield was up 22.2 basis points, while the breakeven was 17.4 basis points lower.

Risk assets treated the change as an improvement in the prospective growth-inflation balance rather than a warning of imminent economic weakness. The S&P 500 gained 1.75%, the Nasdaq 100 rose 3.29% and the PHLX Semiconductor Index jumped 7.91%. The VIX fell 12.51% to 19.44, while investment-grade, high-yield and emerging-market bond funds all advanced. The dollar index eased 0.09% and gold slipped 0.44%.

The session nevertheless left several constraints intact. Trump has previously suggested that a settlement was near without producing a durable agreement, and Iranian approval of the latest terms was not established. The wholesale-price data showed that energy was already passing through supply chains, with final-demand goods prices surging 2.8% and a measure designed to remove volatile food, energy and trade margins still rising sharply. The European Central Bank responded to the same global shock by raising rates for the first time since 2023, while the Fed approached its June meeting with elevated U.S. inflation, only incremental labor softening and a new chair whose communication strategy remains uncertain.

## Oil Relief Overcomes Hot Producer Prices

The Treasury market’s initial response to the economic data was constrained by the breadth of the producer-price increase. Final-demand prices rose 1.1% in May, matching April’s monthly advance and lifting the annual rate to 6.5%. The monthly result exceeded the 0.7% consensus and was not solely the product of one narrow category.

Goods prices increased 2.8%, led by a 10.7% rise in energy, while services prices advanced 0.3%. The measure excluding food, energy and trade services rose 0.8% after 0.5% in April, compared with a 0.5% consensus, and was 5.1% higher from a year earlier. The figures strengthened the evidence that the energy shock was moving beyond crude itself into domestic production and distribution costs.

That composition was less reassuring than the preceding consumer-price report, in which core inflation had risen less than forecast. It did not prove that the entire wholesale increase would pass through to consumers, but it deprived the Fed of a uniformly softer inflation sequence before its June 16-17 meeting. The contrast between consumer and producer measures leaves officials assessing whether subdued core consumer inflation is durable or merely lagging a renewed increase in pipeline costs.

Labor data supplied the day’s main domestic counterweight. Initial unemployment claims rose by 4,000 to 229,000 in the week ended June 6, above the 220,000 consensus and the highest reading since February. The 4-week average increased to 219,000 from 214,750. Continuing claims rose by 24,000 to 1.795 million in the week ended May 30 after the previous reading was revised to 1.771 million, while the insured unemployment rate held at 1.2%.

The claims data pointed to some deterioration in both new layoffs and the time required to find work, but the changes were not large enough to establish a decisive break in labor demand. Their importance was in the balance they introduced: the inflation side of the Fed’s mandate received a substantial upside surprise, while the employment side showed a gradual increase in strain rather than the abrupt weakness that would make tighter policy implausible.

Trump’s reversal on Iran changed that balance more forcefully in market prices. Earlier in the day, he had threatened further attacks and the seizure of Iranian oil infrastructure if Tehran did not accept an interim agreement. He later canceled strikes planned for the evening, said discussions had reached Iranian leaders and indicated that the time and place for signing an accord would be announced. Reports did not establish that Tehran had approved a final text, preserving the risk that the diplomatic opening could reverse.

Treasuries had been only about 2 basis points stronger before the announcement. They subsequently rallied by 8 to 11 basis points across maturities as oil fell more than 3% intraday. The move restored yields to levels seen before the strong May employment report on June 5 had pushed investors toward a more hawkish Fed path.

The curve response was restrained because the change affected both policy expectations and longer-duration inflation risk. The 2s10s spread narrowed 0.9 basis point to 39.9 basis points, while 2s30s widened 0.8 basis point to 89.3 basis points. The 5-year led the rally, but the differences among coupon tenors were too small to suggest a wholesale reordering of the curve’s policy and term-premium components.

The decline in breakevens was consistent with lower oil, while the larger fall in real yields reflected more than the mechanical removal of an energy premium. Reduced geopolitical risk improved the probability that the Fed could wait rather than add restraint into a slowing global economy. The simultaneous equity rally reinforced that interpretation: investors marked down the likelihood of an adverse combination of persistent inflation, tighter policy and disrupted activity.

That relief remained conditional. WTI and Brent were down over the week and month, yet their closing levels near $88 and $90 still embodied a substantial energy cost. Producer prices showed that earlier increases were already entering goods and broader underlying measures. A signed agreement that reopens disrupted trade routes would reduce prospective inflation pressure, but it would not reverse price increases already recorded or automatically prevent businesses from passing those costs forward.

The World Bank’s updated global outlook illustrated the economic stakes. It projected world growth of 2.5% in 2026, the weakest pace since the pandemic recession in 2020, after worsening its assessment for two-thirds of economies because the war had disrupted commodity flows and lifted energy and import costs. Emerging economies outside China and India bore the largest deterioration, while China’s forecast was reduced to 4.2% from 4.4%.

The bank characterized the episode as the largest supply shock in more than 50 years and said global growth could fall to 1.3% if energy disruptions became more severe and coincided with substantial financial stress. Those were conditional estimates rather than a prediction that the downside case would occur. They help explain why a credible peace agreement could lower yields through both inflation and real-rate channels even when the latest U.S. data remained too firm to support easing.

## Long-Bond Supply Meets a Fed Liquidity Backstop

Treasury’s $22 billion 30-year reopening produced a mixed demand signal before the geopolitical rally accelerated. The bonds cleared at a 5.020% high yield, below the 5.046% result at the May new issue but above the level indicated in pre-auction trading. The bid-to-cover ratio improved to 2.33 from 2.30, although the higher-than-indicated clearing yield showed that investors still required a concession at the auction itself.

The allocation was more constructive. Direct bidders took 25.31% of accepted competitive tenders, indirect bidders received 59.95% and primary dealers were left with 14.74%. The direct share helped absorb a $22 billion reopening that was smaller than May’s $25 billion new issue. The securities carry a 5.000% coupon, settle June 15 and mature May 15, 2056.

Yields briefly moved higher after the result, but the setback was overtaken by the oil-driven rally. The 30-year yield ultimately fell as much as 9 basis points intraday and finished below 5%. The sequence separated auction execution from the day’s dominant repricing: demand was softer than pre-sale trading implied, yet it was not weak enough to resist a much larger change in the perceived geopolitical and inflation outlook.

The front-end auctions did not show generalized funding stress. Treasury’s $70 billion 4-week bill sale stopped at a 3.595% high rate, down from 3.615% previously, while its bid-to-cover ratio improved to 3.13 from 3.07. Indirect bidders took 70.59%, direct bidders 2.01% and dealers 27.39%. The smaller offering settles June 16 and matures July 14.

The $75.001 billion 8-week auction stopped at an unchanged 3.610% rate, but cover weakened to 2.94 from 3.20. Indirect participation remained high at 69.59%, direct bidders took 2.27% and dealers received 28.14%. The issue also settles June 16 and matures August 11. The contrast between improved 4-week demand and softer 8-week cover argued against treating the two sales as one uniform liquidity signal.

Federal Reserve reserve-management operations supplied a separate funding development. The New York Fed said it would purchase about $10 billion of Treasury bills during the monthly period ending July 13, unchanged from the previous cycle, and conduct about $16.5 billion of reinvestment purchases. The decision maintained support for reserves ahead of an expected increase in Treasury bill supply and a rise in the government’s cash balance above $1 trillion.

The Fed had begun buying about $40 billion of bills a month in December after ending quantitative tightening, then reduced the pace to $25 billion in April and $10 billion in May. Holding the amount steady interrupted that rapid deceleration without signaling a return to the earlier pace. New York Fed markets chief Roberto Perli had said purchases could be adjusted in either direction to keep reserves ample.

Current funding conditions were benign. Bank reserves rose by $65.8 billion to $3.111 trillion in the week through June 10, up from $2.85 trillion at the end of 2025, while money-market fund assets reached records and cash remained abundant relative to collateral. The decision to maintain purchases was therefore precautionary, aimed at the future reserve drain associated with Treasury cash management rather than a response to realized market dysfunction.

Cash Treasury activity increased as yields fell. FINRA recorded $1.188 trillion of par activity across 415,918 trades, 6.8% more than in the previous session. Nominal-coupon activity rose 13.3% to $926.4 billion, including increases of 24.6% in securities with more than 3 and up to 5 years remaining and 31.4% in the sector above 7 and through 10 years. TIPS activity declined 33% to $31.9 billion.

The turnover confirms that the rally occurred during an active session, particularly in the belly and benchmark 10-year sector, but the aggregates do not identify whether customers were net buyers or sellers. The price evidence supplied the clearer conclusion: the Iran announcement overwhelmed a hot inflation release, a somewhat soft long-bond stop and substantial coupon trading because it changed the expected persistence of the energy shock.

## The ECB Opens a New Tightening Cycle

The ECB raised its deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.25%, its first increase in almost 3 years and the first tightening response by a major central bank to the Iran-related energy shock. The decision was unanimous and broadly anticipated, leaving the substance of President Christine Lagarde’s explanation and the possibility of further increases as the more consequential information for European duration.

Lagarde said the shock was broadening through the economy, with both direct and indirect costs appearing, and rejected the characterization of the move as preemptive. The ECB described the outlook as one of upside inflation risks and downside growth risks, with the ultimate effects depending on the duration and intensity of the energy shock and the extent of second-round transmission.

The bank’s new projections showed faster consumer-price growth in 2026 and 2027 before a return toward 2% in 2028. Lagarde said energy prices would lift inflation further during the summer and keep it well above target through the first half of 2027. At the same time, the conflict was weighing on activity and surveys indicated a slowdown, particularly in services.

European bonds retained gains after the decision, with the 10-year benchmark yield reported 3 basis points lower at 3.05%. The market response did not reject the hike; it reflected the tension between the higher near-term policy path and weaker prospective growth, along with the same decline in oil that drove Treasuries later in the U.S. session.

Officials left open a second increase as early as July. September, when the next quarterly forecasts are available, remained the prevailing expectation, but people familiar with Governing Council discussions said July could not be excluded if inflation concerns persisted. Improvement in the geopolitical and energy outlook could still produce a pause.

The IMF endorsed further tightening while preserving a growth qualification. Its baseline assumed 50 basis points of cumulative increases during 2026 and projected euro-area inflation at 2.8%, up from its prior 2.4% estimate. Staff said a slightly more restrictive stance might be needed if incoming data followed that baseline, with faster or larger moves warranted if energy prices and inflation expectations exceeded it.

The fund also reduced its euro-area growth forecast to 0.9% from 1.1%. It said a larger deterioration in financial conditions and demand could widen the output gap and reduce the need for tightening. That condition matters because the ECB is responding to a supply disturbance whose inflationary effect argues for higher rates even as its drag on household purchasing power and business activity argues for restraint.

Political opposition emerged quickly. Italian Deputy Prime Minister Antonio Tajani said the increase did not help and argued that credit should remain accessible when inflation stemmed from external factors. Italy also objected during a meeting of euro-area finance ministers, as did Portugal, whose finance minister described the signal as unnecessary while acknowledging the ECB’s independence.

Norway presented a similar conflict with a different current policy setting. Norges Bank’s regional-network survey showed businesses expecting output growth of 0.2% in the second quarter and 0.3% in the third, compared with a prior forecast of 0.4% for the second quarter. Slightly fewer firms reported capacity constraints and recruitment difficulties also eased.

The survey reduced pressure for another increase at the June 18 meeting after core inflation unexpectedly reached a 4-month high in May. Employment was still expected to increase modestly, and businesses raised their wage-growth forecast to 4.5%, matching the central bank’s projection. The evidence therefore weakened the immediate case for a second consecutive hike without removing the wage and imported-price pressures behind the debate.

In the U.K., the next policy decision acquired an added fiscal risk. Investors were preparing for volatility around the June 18 Makerfield by-election, which could give Labour politician Andy Burnham a route into Parliament and a potential challenge to Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Managers expressed particular concern about long-dated gilts because Burnham’s fiscal approach remained difficult to assess.

Britain’s budget deficit reached £24.3 billion in April, its largest for that month in 6 years, while the OECD projected debt rising to 105.4% of gross domestic product by 2027 from 98.8% in 2023. Some investors said 30-year gilt yields would need to rise nearly 40 basis points or reach about 6% before adequately compensating them for the uncertainty. A Burnham loss could bring relief if it strengthened confidence in existing fiscal rules, although a Reform UK victory would introduce a different set of institutional and policy questions.

## Credit Rewards Defined Funding, but Rejects Weak Structures

Corporate credit remained open to large borrowers, but the strongest reception went to issuers that either clarified future funding or paid explicitly for risk. Citigroup’s banking arm sold $6.25 billion of investment-grade bonds in four parts, ranging from 2 to 6 years, in its first high-grade transaction of 2026. Pricing on the longest tranche tightened to 67 basis points over Treasuries from initial talk near 95 basis points.

The notes were operating-company debt issued by Citibank rather than holding-company obligations and were expected to carry ratings of Aa3 from Moody’s, A+ from S&P and AA- from Fitch. Citi had lagged the other largest Wall Street banks, which had already raised more than $120 billion during the year, after changes to a long-term-debt capital rule reduced its urgency to issue.

Oracle’s bonds rallied even as its shares fell sharply following higher-than-expected data-center spending. The company said it did not expect to issue more debt during calendar 2026 and outlined a plan to raise $40 billion of debt and equity during its new fiscal year, including a previously announced $20 billion at-the-market equity program.

Oracle’s 3.65% bond due in 2041 tightened by 15 basis points to a spread of 200 basis points as of noon in New York, while its 6.9% issue due in 2052 tightened 12 basis points to 209 basis points. The cost of 5-year default protection fell as much as 3.4 basis points to 155.7 basis points.

The reaction reflected relief about the boundary around new borrowing rather than lower capital needs. Oracle spent about $16.5 billion in the quarter ended May 31, taking full-year capital expenditure to $55.7 billion, above its $50 billion projection. Net capital spending in the new fiscal year was expected to reach about $70 billion. Greater use of customer prepayments and customers supplying their own processors was viewed as reducing near-term cash requirements even as the investment program remained exceptionally large.

CoreWeave demonstrated that global demand also extended to lower-rated AI infrastructure. The company sold €2 billion of 6-year euro bonds at an 8.5% yield and $1.25 billion of 6-year dollar notes at 9.625%. Orders for the euro tranche exceeded €7 billion, giving a U.S. AI infrastructure company its first euro-denominated junk-bond transaction of this kind.

The deal broadened CoreWeave’s funding base but did not eliminate its financial risk. The company was expected to invest almost $35 billion and burn nearly $26 billion of cash during the year. Before the new sale, it had issued $6.5 billion of junk-rated dollar bonds since May 2025, $6.6 billion of convertible notes and a $3.1 billion loan secured by customer contracts for chips. Moody’s rated it Ba3, S&P B+ and Fitch BB-.

Hanuman Wind Power encountered the other side of that selectivity. The Hong Kong-based unit of Thailand’s Energy Absolute postponed its proposed green junk bond for a second time after extending order-taking by an extra day. The latest notes offered a yield in the mid-to-high 9% range, yet investors remained concerned about governance at the parent and about the relative value of a 15-year structure after the rise in Treasury yields.

Part of the proposed proceeds was intended for Energy Absolute, whose founder and former executives had been accused of fraud by Thailand’s market regulator. The issuer had also postponed an offering in February. The repeated withdrawal showed that a high single-digit yield and a renewable-energy label were insufficient when concerns centered on governance, structural exposure to the parent and long maturity.

Danantara, Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund, completed the debut transaction that had been under scrutiny during the country’s market turmoil. It raised $1.5 billion through equal $750 million 5- and 10-year tranches. The 5-year notes priced at 5.35%, and both tranches tightened by about 35 basis points from initial price talk.

Demand was less than twice the offering for each tranche, below the 3-times-or-greater books seen on many recent Asian deals, but the completed sale was still an important funding result after Indonesia’s currency, stocks and local bonds had come under pressure. The notes traded higher in subsequent Asian dealings. The transaction established that Danantara could access global dollars, though it did not erase policy and governance concerns reflected elsewhere in Indonesian assets.

The fund was also considering a local-currency offering with coupons below prevailing market rates. That prospective structure revived unease associated with earlier below-market “Patriot Bonds,” making the distinction between successful international execution and the terms of any domestically directed financing important.

Other borrowers remained in earlier stages. Dangote Petroleum Refinery was seeking as much as $1 billion through a private debt placement aimed at foreign investors while also preparing an initial public offering and expanding a refinery capable of processing as much as 700,000 barrels a day. Investor meetings were continuing and the transaction was not assured. Zimbabwe was separately discussing a $150 million African Development Bank loan as part of a wider effort to clear arrears and restructure about $23 billion of debt, after being excluded from international capital markets since 1999.

## Asian Rates Separate Energy Exposure From Domestic Credibility

Indonesia’s local markets remained the clearest case in which lower global oil risk could not immediately repair domestic confidence. The benchmark 10-year yield rose 10 basis points to 7.45% on Thursday, near its highest since 2022, while the 5-year yield added 3 basis points. The rupiah weakened 0.2% and the equity benchmark closed 0.3% lower after falling as much as 2% intraday.

The renewed decline followed only a brief rebound after officials explained their efforts to defend the currency. Bank Indonesia had accepted higher bond yields, tightened liquidity and raised rates by 75 basis points since May, including an off-cycle 25-basis-point increase. Analysts still saw room for an additional 25 to 50 basis points of tightening, with another move widely expected at the scheduled meeting on June 18.

Foreign investors had withdrawn a net $3.9 billion from Indonesian stocks and $597 million from bonds during the year. The rupiah was about 7% weaker against the dollar and the equity index more than 30% lower. High oil prices had threatened the trade balance and inflation outlook, but the persistent weakness also reflected concern about fiscal policy, governance and President Prabowo Subianto’s interventionist agenda.

Danantara’s completed dollar sale and the rupiah’s subsequent improvement showed that confidence was not uniformly absent. The currency finished its best week since October after the surprise rate increase and strengthened through 18,000 per dollar, while Indonesian stocks also advanced on Friday. The recovery nevertheless followed a severe drawdown and did not by itself resolve the local sovereign market’s demand for additional yield and policy clarity.

Thailand offered a contrasting regional rates configuration. Its 10-year yield stood nearly 110 basis points above the 2-year yield, close to the steepest curve in emerging Asia and near the widest gap since November 2022. Unlike countries tightening to defend currencies, Thailand’s weak economy and softer May inflation allowed investors to expect an extended pause from the Bank of Thailand.

Foreign investors had bought about $342 million of Thai bonds during the quarter, reversing part of approximately $1 billion of March outflows. The 10-year yield had retreated from an over 1-year high of 2.4% reached in May. A Bloomberg model estimated the yield was roughly 40 basis points above fair value after rising almost 60 basis points since the conflict escalated, compared with about 18 basis points implied by U.S. yields, the dollar, regional equities and oil.

That valuation assessment was model-based rather than a realized policy signal. It nevertheless captured why long Thai bonds could perform differently from Indonesian duration even under the same regional energy shock: baht swaps had not fully priced a quarter-point increase over 6 months, while swaps in India and South Korea incorporated at least 50 basis points of tightening.

Peru also preserved policy stability amid political uncertainty. The central bank held its benchmark rate at 4.25% for a ninth month, matching the expectation of 13 economists, while one had forecast a 25-basis-point increase. Inflation in Lima slowed to 3.91% from 4.01%, supporting the bank’s view that pressure from a domestic gas shortage, global oil and crop damage could prove temporary even though inflation remained above its 1%-3% target range.

The presidential runoff remained unresolved with 98.2% of votes counted and Keiko Fujimori and Roberto Sánchez separated by fewer than 1,000 ballots. Hundreds of thousands of challenged votes could delay official results until July. The political uncertainty moved the currency during the week, but the central bank’s hold distinguished the monetary decision from the unresolved election.

Japan’s June meeting remained highly consequential, but Governor Kazuo Ueda’s expected absence shifted attention from the likely decision to its communication. Ueda was expected to provide his views in a statement without voting, Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino was to act as chair and Deputy Governor Shinichi Uchida was scheduled to conduct the press conference.

Overnight-index swaps briefly lowered the probability of a quarter-point increase to about 73% before returning to near-full pricing. Investors were therefore not treating Ueda’s hospitalization as a fundamental change in the likely rate decision. The uncertainty concerned how clearly Uchida would describe the possibility and pace of subsequent tightening, a distinction with direct relevance for the yen and super-long JGBs.

## Forward Market Significance

The immediate U.S. test is the preliminary University of Michigan survey at 10:00 ET on June 12. The sentiment index is expected to rise to 46.1 from May’s final 44.8. Its household inflation-expectations measures will be more important for rates after producer prices showed a broad monthly increase and oil fell on diplomatic hopes. Lower expectations would support the judgment that the energy shock has not become entrenched; renewed increases would leave the Fed with less comfort from the decline in market breakevens.

U.K. April gross domestic product arrives earlier on June 12, with a 0.1% monthly contraction expected after 0.3% growth in March. The release will update the activity side of the Bank of England’s June 18 decision and the gilt market’s assessment of how much restraint the economy can absorb while energy inflation and domestic political risk remain elevated.

June 15 brings U.S. industrial production, expected to rise 0.1% in May after 0.9%, and capacity utilization after a 76.1% reading. The data are the final major hard-activity update before the FOMC meeting. The same day, Treasury settles $58 billion of 3-year notes, $39 billion of 10-year notes and $22 billion of 30-year bonds, creating $119 billion of gross coupon settlement. Auctions of $89 billion in 13-week bills and $77 billion in 26-week bills will test front-end absorption alongside that balance-sheet event.

China releases May industrial production, retail sales and fixed-asset investment on June 16. The prior readings were 4.1% annual industrial growth, 3.2% retail-sales growth and a 1.6% year-to-date decline in fixed-asset investment. The package will show whether domestic demand and fiscal transmission are strong enough to offset the external energy and trade shock across Chinese and regional duration.

The BOJ decides the same day after its June 15-16 meeting. A 25-basis-point increase to around 1% forms the prevailing expectation, but the market’s larger test is the guidance delivered without Ueda at the press conference. Clear communication on subsequent tightening could reinforce pressure on JGBs and the yen’s rate differential; ambiguity would increase the volatility attached to a decision that is already heavily priced.

The Reserve Bank of Australia also decides June 16, with a hold at 4.35% forming the baseline after its May increase. In the U.S., import and export prices and housing starts arrive at 08:30 ET, followed by a $65 billion 6-week bill auction and a $13 billion 20-year bond reopening. Trade prices will indicate whether the energy and goods shock is broadening, while the 20-year sale will test duration demand after the 30-year reopening cleared above its pre-auction indication.

May retail sales at 08:30 ET on June 17 precede the FOMC decision at 14:00 and Chair Kevin Warsh’s first post-meeting press conference at 14:30. Sales are expected to increase between 0.5% and 0.6% after an initial 0.5% April gain. Resilient spending alongside firm producer prices would make it harder to validate the market’s postponement of a fully priced increase into 2027; weaker consumption would reinforce the claims data and the growth relief embedded in lower real yields.

The Fed is expected to leave the target range at 3.50%-3.75%, making the Summary of Economic Projections and Warsh’s communication the main events. Investors will be watching whether the new chair retains the dot plot and established degree of forward guidance, and how he links balance-sheet policy to the rate outlook. Less communication could add volatility even if the decision itself is unchanged.

June 18 brings decisions from Bank Indonesia, the Swiss National Bank, Norges Bank, the Bank of England and the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. Indonesia’s meeting will test whether the off-cycle defense of the rupiah is followed by another 25-basis-point increase from 5.50%. Norges Bank must weigh slower business activity against firm core inflation and 4.5% wage expectations, while the Bank of England must judge energy inflation against softer growth and the outcome of the Makerfield vote.

Oil remains the condition capable of changing all of those judgments before they are made. A signed agreement that materially reduces supply disruption would extend the decline in energy inflation and give central banks more room to differentiate according to domestic growth and wages. A failure of the negotiations would return markets to the combination that preceded Thursday’s rally: high crude prices, broadening pipeline inflation and pressure for additional tightening despite a weakening global outlook.

section_summaries.summary: Iran diplomacy displaced the producer-price shock as the session’s dominant force, sending Treasury yields sharply lower and pushing the next fully priced Fed increase into Q1 2027. Both the 10-year real yield and breakeven declined, while equities rallied and volatility fell, signaling relief from the prospective mix of energy inflation, tighter policy and weaker growth.

section_summaries.market_read: Lower oil reduced breakevens, while geopolitical relief gave the Fed more scope to wait despite firm pipeline inflation.
section_summaries.section_title: Oil Relief Overcomes Hot Producer Prices
section_summaries.summary: May producer prices rose 1.1%, with goods up 2.8% and energy up 10.7%, showing that the energy shock was moving into production and distribution costs. Higher jobless claims added only gradual labor strain, but Trump’s cancellation of planned Iran strikes drove oil lower and turned a modest Treasury gain into an 8-to-11-basis-point rally across maturities.

section_summaries.market_read: Active Treasury turnover confirmed a broad repricing, but aggregate volumes did not identify whether customers were net buyers or sellers.
section_summaries.section_title: Long-Bond Supply Meets a Fed Liquidity Backstop
section_summaries.summary: The $22 billion 30-year reopening cleared above its pre-auction indication despite improved cover, but its brief yield setback was overwhelmed by the oil-driven rally. Bill auctions gave mixed demand signals, while the New York Fed kept monthly bill purchases near $10 billion to preserve ample reserves ahead of heavier Treasury cash needs rather than to address current funding stress.

section_summaries.market_read: European bond gains reflected the tension between a higher near-term policy path and weaker prospective growth.
section_summaries.next_check: Whether persistent inflation produces another ECB increase in July or lower oil allows officials to pause.
section_summaries.section_title: The ECB Opens a New Tightening Cycle
section_summaries.summary: The ECB unanimously raised its deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.25%, its first increase in almost 3 years, as the Iran-related energy shock broadened through the economy. A July increase remained possible, but weaker growth and lower oil could support a pause. Norway’s softer business survey reduced pressure for another immediate hike, while U.K. long gilts faced added fiscal uncertainty around the June 18 Makerfield by-election.

section_summaries.market_read: Danantara’s completed $1.5 billion dollar sale established market access without resolving wider Indonesian policy and governance concerns.
section_summaries.section_title: Credit Rewards Defined Funding, but Rejects Weak Structures
section_summaries.summary: Credit markets rewarded borrowers that defined their funding needs or paid clearly for risk. Citibank placed $6.25 billion across four tranches, Oracle bonds rallied after it ruled out more 2026 debt, and CoreWeave drew strong demand for high-yield euro and dollar notes. Hanuman Wind Power postponed its green bond again as governance, parent exposure and a 15-year maturity outweighed its high yield.

section_summaries.market_read: Regional duration separated according to domestic credibility, growth and wage pressures rather than moving uniformly with oil.
section_summaries.section_title: Asian Rates Separate Energy Exposure From Domestic Credibility
section_summaries.summary: Lower global oil risk did not immediately repair Indonesia’s local-market confidence: its 10-year yield rose 10 basis points to 7.45% as fiscal, governance and currency concerns persisted. Thailand’s weak economy and softer inflation supported an extended policy pause and a steep curve, while Peru held at 4.25%. In Japan, the expected hike remained heavily priced, but Governor Kazuo Ueda’s absence increased uncertainty around subsequent guidance.

The next tests span U.S. inflation expectations, activity, Treasury settlement and central-bank communication. Michigan expectations will show whether the energy shock is becoming entrenched; the June 17 FOMC will test the market’s shift of a fully priced hike into 2027; and BOJ guidance without Ueda will determine whether a heavily priced decision creates further volatility. Oil diplomacy remains the condition capable of changing those judgments first.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries rally as Iran diplomacy and lower oil outweigh a broad producer-price surge
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied broadly after President Donald Trump canceled planned strikes against Iran and said an agreement to end the war could soon be announced. The 2-year yield fell 8.2 basis points to 4.063%, the 5-year dropped 9.6 basis points to 4.185%, the 10-year declined 9.1 basis points to 4.462% and the 30-year shed 7.4 basis points to 4.956%. WTI fell 2.58% to $87.71 and Brent lost 2.92% to $90.38, pushing the next fully priced Fed increase from December into Q1 2027.

The rally overcame a broad inflation surprise rather than following benign data. May producer prices rose 1.1% from April and 6.5% from a year earlier, while the measure excluding food, energy and trade services increased 0.8%. Initial jobless claims rose to 229,000, adding a softer labor signal without establishing a decisive break in demand. Lower oil reduced inflation compensation, while the larger decline in real yields reflected improved scope for the Fed to wait rather than tighten into a slowing global economy.

Equities rallied and volatility fell as investors marked down the risk of persistent inflation, tighter policy and disrupted activity. Relief remained conditional because Iran had not been shown to have approved a final agreement, earlier energy increases were already entering production costs, and the ECB raised rates by 25 basis points in response to broadening inflation pressure.
